title: Unsupported backend-tool bundles resolve storage without emitting any streaming failure event
reasoning: When a prepared bundle contains any backend-executed tool, send_tools marks the bundle failed in result storage and returns without yielding a ToolBundleEvent, ToolCallEvent, ToolOutputEvent, or other streaming error event. Consumers that rely on the stream rather than result_storage get a silent stop for this unsupported path, while other preparation failures emit per-tool failure envelopes before returning. That creates an observable contract mismatch in the sending phase: a rejected execution path is recorded internally but not surfaced through the normal streaming event channel.
recommendation: Emit an explicit streaming failure event for the unsupported backend-tool bundle path before returning, preferably using the same envelope/error-event shape as preparation failures or a bundle-level failure event if one exists. Keep result_storage resolution as the internal completion mechanism, but do not make it the only visible signal.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for this feature, and the current excerpt has no test evidence asserting stream behavior for rejected mixed/backend bundles.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a sender test with a prepared bundle containing a backend-target tool and assert that send_tools yields a visible failure event and resolves the bundle result as failed.
minimumFixScope: ToolSender.send_tools unsupported backend bundle branch, plus focused sender tests.
